Literature-informed assessment: The statement blends continued accommodation with measured normalization. The average-inflation-targeting language and data-dependent guidance align with inflation-forecast-targeting frameworks (Svensson; Svensson and Woodford), aiming to keep expectations anchored near 2 percent. Keeping the policy rate at the ELB while beginning to taper is broadly consistent with rule-like behavior that stabilizes inflation and the output gap over time (Taylor principle; Clarida, Galí, and Gertler; Rudebusch), while the taper acknowledges evidence that QE primarily works via term premia and financial conditions (Bernanke and coauthors). At the same time, risks from elevated inflation and supply constraints echo time-inconsistency and mismeasurement concerns (Barro-Gordon; Orphanides) and possible inflation inertia (Galí and Gertler), warranting vigilance if “transitory” pressures persist.

Overall tone: constructive but cautious.

Key sentence: “In light of the substantial further progress the economy has made toward the Committee’s goals since last December, the Committee decided to begin reducing the monthly pace of its net asset purchases.”
